class.name: LightmapGI
class.brief_description: Computes and stores baked lightmaps for fast global illumination.
class.description: The [LightmapGI] node is used to compute and store baked lightmaps. Lightmaps are used to provide high-quality indirect lighting with very little light leaking. [LightmapGI] can also provide rough reflections using spherical harmonics if [member directional] is enabled. Dynamic objects receive baked indirect lighting from probes placed in [LightProbeVolume] nodes under a [LightProbeSystem]. The editor can bake lightmaps and probes together, only lightmaps, or only probes. Partial bakes retain the other lighting data and its appearance. Texture lightmaps use [LightmapGIData]; probe lighting and its exposure use [LightProbeData] assigned to the probe systems. Probe placement controls and lighting preview belong to the probe nodes. Selecting LightmapGI does not display probes. No probes are generated automatically by LightmapGI. The downside is that lightmaps are fully static and cannot be baked in an exported project. Baking a [LightmapGI] node is also slower compared to [VoxelGI]. [b]Procedural generation:[/b] Lightmap baking functionality is only available in the editor. This means [LightmapGI] is not suited to procedurally generated or user-built levels. For procedurally generated or user-built levels, use [VoxelGI] or SDFGI instead (see [member Environment.sdfgi_enabled]). [b]Performance:[/b] [LightmapGI] provides the best possible run-time performance for global illumination. It is suitable for low-end hardware including integrated graphics and mobile devices. [b]Note:[/b] Due to how lightmaps work, most properties only have a visible effect once lightmaps are baked again. [b]Note:[/b] Lightmap baking on [CSGShape3D]s and [PrimitiveMesh]es is not supported, as these cannot store UV2 data required for baking. [b]Note:[/b] If no custom lightmappers are installed, [LightmapGI] can only be baked from devices that support the Forward+ or Mobile renderers. [b]Note:[/b] The [LightmapGI] node only bakes light data for child nodes of its parent. Nodes further up the hierarchy of the scene will not be baked. Runtime adjustments ([member energy], [member tint], [member saturation], [member contrast], [member shadows], [member midtones], and [member highlights]) only affect the baked lightmap textures of static geometry. Dynamic object probes, other lighting and shadowmask textures are unaffected. Tonal ranges are evaluated in the baked linear HDR space before the current camera exposure, so their response depends on the exposure used for baking. [b]Note:[/b] Runtime adjustments are sent to the rendering resource of [member light_data]. Nodes sharing the same [LightmapGIData] also share these adjustments; use separate data resources for independently adjusted lightmaps. Runtime tonal grading also supports independently adjustable tonal range boundaries and per-range tint, saturation, and contrast. Weights are determined before per-range adjustments so the controls do not change their own range selection. Tonal controls, including the three range tints, are approximated on dynamic object probes by spherical harmonics projection.

members.member: Enables lightmap color adjustments in Forward+. The editor applies them per pixel to the original texture; the game uses a cached derived texture. An additional packed positive HDR texture is generated on the GPU when controls or the original texture change; stable frames only sample the cached result. Controls include energy, tint, saturation, contrast and tonal ranges. Directional lightmaps process only the L0 color layer; normals and dynamic object probes use their original data. Direction layers are copied without grading into the reduced precision format. Generated specular shares the adjusted L0 through the original material sampling path. Disabled or neutral settings use the original texture. Settings are shared by nodes using the same LightmapGIData. The cache uses 4 bytes per texel across all layers and requires packed HDR sampling/storage support. Signed BC6H sources or unsupported devices retain the original lightmap. Regeneration occurs only when controls or the source change. No rebaking is required.

The maximum distance, in world units, at which geometry occludes a texel for baked ambient occlusion. Occlusion decreases smoothly to zero at this distance. Only effective if [member bake_ao] is [code]true[/code].

How strongly baked ambient occlusion affects direct lighting. At [code]0.0[/code], AO only affects indirect lighting. At [code]1.0[/code], AO affects direct and indirect lighting equally. Only effective if [member bake_ao] is [code]true[/code].
The number of hemisphere rays traced per lightmap texel for ambient occlusion. Higher values reduce noise at the cost of longer bake times. Only effective if [member bake_ao] is [code]true[/code].

The strength of baked ambient occlusion. A value of [code]0.0[/code] has no effect, [code]1.0[/code] applies the computed distance-weighted occlusion, and values above [code]1.0[/code] exaggerate it. Only effective if [member bake_ao] is [code]true[/code].

If [code]true[/code], traces local ambient occlusion and stores it directly in the generated lightmap. This has no additional run-time texture or sampling cost, but increases bake time. This is an artistic adjustment that adds occlusion on top of the baked indirect lighting. Transparent surfaces attenuate occlusion according to their opacity, subject to [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/bake_performance/max_transparency_rays].

The bias to use when computing shadows. Increasing [member bias] can fix shadow acne on the resulting baked lightmap, but can introduce peter-panning (shadows not connecting to their casters). Real-time [Light3D] shadows are not affected by this [member bias] property.

The energy multiplier for each bounce. Higher values will make indirect lighting brighter. A value of [code]1.0[/code] represents physically accurate behavior, but higher values can be used to make indirect lighting propagate more visibly when using a low number of bounces. This can be used to speed up bake times by lowering the number of [member bounces] then increasing [member bounce_indirect_energy]. [b]Note:[/b] [member bounce_indirect_energy] only has an effect if [member bounces] is set to a value greater than or equal to [code]1[/code].

Number of light bounces that are taken into account during baking. Higher values result in brighter, more realistic lighting, at the cost of longer bake times. If set to [code]0[/code], only environment lighting, direct light and emissive lighting is baked.

The [CameraAttributes] resource that specifies exposure levels to bake at. Auto-exposure and non exposure properties will be ignored. Exposure settings should be used to reduce the dynamic range present when baking. If exposure is too high, the [LightmapGI] will have banding artifacts or may have over-exposure artifacts.

Runtime luminance contrast of baked lighting, with a fixed pivot at linear luminance [code]0.18[/code]. [code]1.0[/code] preserves contrast; smaller values reduce it and larger values increase it. The range is [code]0.0[/code] to [code]4.0[/code]. Preserves HDR values and leaves completely black lighting black. Does not require rebaking.

Shows the selected tonal weight in Forward+. In the editor, the mask is displayed directly, tinted blue where Lower acts and orange where Upper acts (see [member shadows_lower] and [member shadows_upper]), independently of material color, directional modulation, other lighting and fog. Camera and auto exposure are canceled like for editor gizmos; tonemapping and screen effects still apply. Weights use original L0 luminance normalized between the texture minimum and maximum, before adjustments. In game, this mode shows the lightmap without adjustments. Settings are shared by nodes using the same LightmapGIData.

The distance in pixels from which the denoiser samples. Lower values preserve more details, but may give blotchy results if the lightmap quality is not high enough. Only effective if [member use_denoiser] is [code]true[/code] and [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/denoising/denoiser] is set to JNLM.

The strength of denoising step applied to the generated lightmaps. Only effective if [member use_denoiser] is [code]true[/code] and [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/denoising/denoiser] is set to JNLM.

If [code]true[/code], bakes lightmaps to contain directional information as spherical harmonics. This results in more realistic lighting appearance, especially with normal mapped materials and for lights that have their direct light baked ([member Light3D.light_bake_mode] set to [constant Light3D.BAKE_STATIC] and with [member Light3D.editor_only] set to [code]false[/code]). The directional information is also used to provide rough reflections for static and dynamic objects. This has a small run-time performance cost as the shader has to perform more work to interpret the direction information from the lightmap. Directional lightmaps also take longer to bake and result in larger file sizes. [b]Note:[/b] The property's name has no relationship with [DirectionalLight3D]. [member directional] works with all light types.
Runtime energy multiplier for baked lighting. A value of [code]0.0[/code] disables its contribution and [code]1.0[/code] preserves the baked energy. Does not require rebaking.
The color to use for environment lighting. Only effective if [member environment_mode] is [constant ENVIRONMENT_MODE_CUSTOM_COLOR].

The energy multiplier for the custom sky or color. Only effective if [member environment_mode] is [constant ENVIRONMENT_MODE_CUSTOM_SKY] or [constant ENVIRONMENT_MODE_CUSTOM_COLOR]. This is multiplied by [member environment_energy].
The sky to use as a source of environment lighting. Only effective if [member environment_mode] is [constant ENVIRONMENT_MODE_CUSTOM_SKY].

The energy multiplier for environment lighting during baking, regardless of whether the source is the scene's [Environment], a custom sky, or a custom color. A value of [code]0.0[/code] removes the environment's contribution, [code]1.0[/code] preserves its original intensity, and higher values increase it. Does not affect direct light or emissive material energy. Changing this property requires baking again to take effect. Has no effect if [member environment_mode] is [constant ENVIRONMENT_MODE_DISABLED].
The environment mode to use when baking lightmaps.

Runtime exposure adjustment for bright baked lighting, in stops, from [code]-4.0[/code] to [code]4.0[/code]. Positive values brighten and negative values darken. The highlight weight increases smoothly between [member tonal_highlights_start] and [member tonal_midtones_end], using luminance normalized between the original texture minimum and maximum. Preserves HDR values. Does not require rebaking.

Input luminance mapped to black in this tonal range. Raising it deepens shadows. The value is kept at least 0.001 below the white point. A value of 0 is neutral. Levels use the maximum luminance of the original lightmap texture as white (1), preserve RGB proportions, and use the original tonal masks. No rebake is required.

Runtime contrast multiplier for the highlights range, from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]4.0[/code]. [code]1.0[/code] is neutral. The three range controls blend smoothly, then multiply global [member contrast], with the combined exponent capped at [code]4.0[/code]. The pivot is fixed at linear luminance [code]0.18[/code]. Does not require rebaking.
Inspector alias for [member highlights], expressed in exposure stops. Both properties modify the same value; scenes serialize [member highlights] for compatibility.

Adjusts intermediate luminance after the black and white points using a power of 1 / Gamma. Values above 1 brighten the range; values below 1 darken it. A value of 1 is neutral. Levels use the maximum luminance of the original lightmap texture as white (1), preserve RGB proportions, and use the original tonal masks. No rebake is required.

Stops added to the darker part of the highlights range only, from [code]-4.0[/code] to [code]4.0[/code]. The effect is strongest at the range's dark end and fades to zero at its bright end, so it brightens or darkens only that part without clipping. Positive values brighten, negative values darken. [member debug_mode] shows this part in blue. Does not require rebaking.

Runtime saturation multiplier for the highlights range, from [code]0.0[/code] (grayscale) to [code]4.0[/code]. [code]1.0[/code] is neutral. The three range controls blend smoothly; ranges are selected from the texture color after global saturation and before per-range adjustments. Does not require rebaking.

Runtime color multiplier for the highlights range of baked lighting. Converted from sRGB to linear space; alpha is ignored. White is neutral. The three range tints blend smoothly using the luminance ranges defined by the four tonal range boundaries. Applies after per-range saturation and contrast and before global [member tint] and [member energy]. Does not require rebaking.

Stops added to the brighter part of the highlights range only, from [code]-4.0[/code] to [code]4.0[/code]. The effect is strongest at the range's bright end and fades to zero at its dark end, so it brightens or darkens only that part without clipping. Positive values brighten, negative values darken. [member debug_mode] shows this part in orange. Does not require rebaking.

Input luminance mapped to white in this tonal range. Lowering it brightens the range. The value is kept at least 0.001 above the black point. A value of 1 is neutral. Values above white retain HDR headroom. Levels use the maximum luminance of the original lightmap texture as white (1), preserve RGB proportions, and use the original tonal masks. No rebake is required.

Maximum luminance of a single indirect lighting sample while baking. Clamping removes fireflies caused by rays hitting small bright emissive surfaces or a bright sun in the environment, at the cost of slightly darkening very bright indirect light. Values around [code]10.0[/code] are a good starting point. [code]0.0[/code] disables clamping.
If [code]true[/code], ignore environment lighting when baking lightmaps.
The [LightmapGIData] associated to this [LightmapGI] node. This resource is automatically created after baking, and is not meant to be created manually.

The maximum texture size for the generated texture atlas. Higher values will result in fewer slices being generated, but may not work on all hardware as a result of hardware limitations on texture sizes. Leave [member max_texture_size] at its default value of [code]16384[/code] if unsure.

Runtime exposure adjustment for medium luminance baked lighting, in stops, from [code]-4.0[/code] to [code]4.0[/code]. Positive values brighten and negative values darken. Its weight is the remainder after the smoothly blended [member shadows] and [member highlights] weights. Does not require rebaking.

Input luminance mapped to black in this tonal range. Raising it deepens shadows. The value is kept at least 0.001 below the white point. A value of 0 is neutral. Levels use the maximum luminance of the original lightmap texture as white (1), preserve RGB proportions, and use the original tonal masks. No rebake is required.

Runtime contrast multiplier for the midtones range, from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]4.0[/code]. [code]1.0[/code] is neutral. The three range controls blend smoothly, then multiply global [member contrast], with the combined exponent capped at [code]4.0[/code]. The pivot is fixed at linear luminance [code]0.18[/code]. Does not require rebaking.
Inspector alias for [member midtones], expressed in exposure stops. Both properties modify the same value; scenes serialize [member midtones] for compatibility.

Adjusts intermediate luminance after the black and white points using a power of 1 / Gamma. Values above 1 brighten the range; values below 1 darken it. A value of 1 is neutral. Levels use the maximum luminance of the original lightmap texture as white (1), preserve RGB proportions, and use the original tonal masks. No rebake is required.

Stops added to the darker part of the midtones range only, from [code]-4.0[/code] to [code]4.0[/code]. The effect is strongest at the range's dark end and fades to zero at its bright end, so it brightens or darkens only that part without clipping. Positive values brighten, negative values darken. [member debug_mode] shows this part in blue. Does not require rebaking.

Runtime saturation multiplier for the midtones range, from [code]0.0[/code] (grayscale) to [code]4.0[/code]. [code]1.0[/code] is neutral. The three range controls blend smoothly; ranges are selected from the texture color after global saturation and before per-range adjustments. Does not require rebaking.

Runtime color multiplier for the midtones range of baked lighting. Converted from sRGB to linear space; alpha is ignored. White is neutral. The three range tints blend smoothly using the luminance ranges defined by the four tonal range boundaries. Applies after per-range saturation and contrast and before global [member tint] and [member energy]. Does not require rebaking.

Stops added to the brighter part of the midtones range only, from [code]-4.0[/code] to [code]4.0[/code]. The effect is strongest at the range's bright end and fades to zero at its dark end, so it brightens or darkens only that part without clipping. Positive values brighten, negative values darken. [member debug_mode] shows this part in orange. Does not require rebaking.

Input luminance mapped to white in this tonal range. Lowering it brightens the range. The value is kept at least 0.001 above the black point. A value of 1 is neutral. Values above white retain HDR headroom. Levels use the maximum luminance of the original lightmap texture as white (1), preserve RGB proportions, and use the original tonal masks. No rebake is required.

The quality preset to use when baking lightmaps. This affects bake times, but output file sizes remain mostly identical across quality levels. To further speed up bake times, decrease [member bounces], disable [member use_denoiser] and/or decrease [member texel_scale]. To further increase quality, enable [member supersampling] and/or increase [member texel_scale].

Runtime saturation of baked lighting. [code]0.0[/code] produces grayscale, [code]1.0[/code] preserves the baked color, and larger values increase saturation. Applied before contrast, tonal adjustments, tint, and energy. Does not require rebaking.

The shadowmasking policy to use for directional shadows on static objects that are baked with this [LightmapGI] instance. Shadowmasking allows [DirectionalLight3D] nodes to cast shadows even outside the range defined by their [member DirectionalLight3D.directional_shadow_max_distance] property. This is done by baking a texture that contains a shadowmap for the directional light, then using this texture according to the current shadowmask mode. [b]Note:[/b] The shadowmask texture is only created if [member shadowmask_mode] is not [constant LightmapGIData.SHADOWMASK_MODE_NONE]. To see a difference, you need to bake lightmaps again after switching from [constant LightmapGIData.SHADOWMASK_MODE_NONE] to any other mode.

Runtime exposure adjustment for dark baked lighting, in stops, from [code]-4.0[/code] to [code]4.0[/code]. Positive values brighten and negative values darken. The shadow weight fades out smoothly between [member tonal_midtones_start] and [member tonal_shadows_end], using luminance normalized between the original texture minimum and maximum. Does not create illumination in completely black areas or require rebaking.

Input luminance mapped to black in this tonal range. Raising it deepens shadows. The value is kept at least 0.001 below the white point. A value of 0 is neutral. Levels use the maximum luminance of the original lightmap texture as white (1), preserve RGB proportions, and use the original tonal masks. No rebake is required.

Runtime contrast multiplier for the shadows range, from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]4.0[/code]. [code]1.0[/code] is neutral. The three range controls blend smoothly, then multiply global [member contrast], with the combined exponent capped at [code]4.0[/code]. The pivot is fixed at linear luminance [code]0.18[/code]. Does not require rebaking.
Inspector alias for [member shadows], expressed in exposure stops. Both properties modify the same value; scenes serialize [member shadows] for compatibility.

Adjusts intermediate luminance after the black and white points using a power of 1 / Gamma. Values above 1 brighten the range; values below 1 darken it. A value of 1 is neutral. Levels use the maximum luminance of the original lightmap texture as white (1), preserve RGB proportions, and use the original tonal masks. No rebake is required.

Stops added to the darker part of the shadows range only, from [code]-4.0[/code] to [code]4.0[/code]. The effect is strongest at the range's dark end and fades to zero at its bright end, so it brightens or darkens only that part without clipping. Positive values brighten, negative values darken. [member debug_mode] shows this part in blue. Does not require rebaking.

Runtime saturation multiplier for the shadows range, from [code]0.0[/code] (grayscale) to [code]4.0[/code]. [code]1.0[/code] is neutral. The three range controls blend smoothly; ranges are selected from the texture color after global saturation and before per-range adjustments. Does not require rebaking.

Runtime color multiplier for the shadows range of baked lighting. Converted from sRGB to linear space; alpha is ignored. White is neutral. The three range tints blend smoothly using the luminance ranges defined by the four tonal range boundaries. Applies after per-range saturation and contrast and before global [member tint] and [member energy]. Does not require rebaking.

Stops added to the brighter part of the shadows range only, from [code]-4.0[/code] to [code]4.0[/code]. The effect is strongest at the range's bright end and fades to zero at its dark end, so it brightens or darkens only that part without clipping. Positive values brighten, negative values darken. [member debug_mode] shows this part in orange. Does not require rebaking.

Input luminance mapped to white in this tonal range. Lowering it brightens the range. The value is kept at least 0.001 above the black point. A value of 1 is neutral. Values above white retain HDR headroom. Levels use the maximum luminance of the original lightmap texture as white (1), preserve RGB proportions, and use the original tonal masks. No rebake is required.

The strength of the lightmap's approximated specular lobe. This helps make lightmapped scenes look closer to real-time lighting, which is particularly noticeable for lights that use the [constant Light3D.BAKE_STATIC] bake mode. Only effective if [member directional] is [code]true[/code]. [b]Note:[/b] The lightmap is only able to represent one light direction per texel, which means that the specular direction may appear to be incorrect in certain cases. This can manifest as specular lobes appearing to warp around as the camera moves.

If [code]true[/code], lightmaps are baked with the texel scale multiplied with [member supersampling_factor] and downsampled before saving the lightmap (so the effective texel density is identical to having supersampling disabled). Supersampling provides increased lightmap quality with less noise, smoother shadows and better shadowing of small-scale features in objects. However, it may result in significantly increased bake times and memory usage while baking lightmaps. Padding is automatically adjusted to avoid increasing light leaking.

The factor by which the texel density is multiplied for supersampling. For best results, use an integer value. While fractional values are allowed, they can result in increased light leaking and a blurry lightmap. Higher values may result in better quality, but also increase bake times and memory usage while baking. See [member supersampling] for more information.

Scales the lightmap texel density of all meshes for the current bake. This is a multiplier that builds upon the existing lightmap texel size defined in each imported 3D scene, along with the per-mesh density multiplier (which is designed to be used when the same mesh is used at different scales). Lower values will result in faster bake times. For example, doubling [member texel_scale] doubles the lightmap texture resolution for all objects [i]on each axis[/i], so it will [i]quadruple[/i] the texel count.
Runtime color multiplier for baked lighting. This color is converted from sRGB to linear space; alpha is ignored. White preserves the original color. Does not require rebaking.

Luminance where highlights start contributing and midtones begin fading. Values use baked linear luminance normalized between the original texture minimum and maximum, in the range [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]. Changing a boundary moves adjacent boundaries if necessary to keep transitions ordered and nonzero. Does not change the contrast pivot or require rebaking.

Luminance where midtones stop contributing and highlights reach full weight. Values use baked linear luminance normalized between the original texture minimum and maximum, in the range [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]. Changing a boundary moves adjacent boundaries if necessary to keep transitions ordered and nonzero. Does not change the contrast pivot or require rebaking.

Luminance where midtones start contributing and shadows begin fading. Values use baked linear luminance normalized between the original texture minimum and maximum, in the range [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]. Changing a boundary moves adjacent boundaries if necessary to keep transitions ordered and nonzero. Does not change the contrast pivot or require rebaking.

Stops added to the bottom of the baked luminance range (the 1st percentile of the lightmap) that places the tonal ranges, from [code]-12.0[/code] to [code]12.0[/code]. [code]0.0[/code] uses the baked range. Raise it to ignore the darkest corners so the tonal ranges spread over the visible surfaces. Also moves the levels axis and the contrast pivot, which sits halfway between bottom and top. Use [member debug_mode] to see the result. Does not require rebaking.

Stops added to the top of the baked luminance range (the 99th percentile of the lightmap) that places the tonal ranges, from [code]-12.0[/code] to [code]12.0[/code]. [code]0.0[/code] uses the baked range. In dark scenes lit by a few bright sources, such as a hangar with lamps, lower it to leave the hot spots above the range so shadows, midtones and highlights spread over the rest of the scene. Also moves the levels axis and the contrast pivot, which sits halfway between bottom and top. Use [member debug_mode] to see the result. Does not require rebaking.

Luminance where shadows stop contributing and midtones reach full weight. Values use baked linear luminance normalized between the original texture minimum and maximum, in the range [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]. Changing a boundary moves adjacent boundaries if necessary to keep transitions ordered and nonzero. Does not change the contrast pivot or require rebaking.

Widens both tonal range transitions (shadows to midtones and midtones to highlights) by this many stops, split evenly on each side, from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]8.0[/code]. [code]0.0[/code] uses the boundaries as set. Because it is measured in stops, it keeps transitions soft when [member tonal_range_bottom] and [member tonal_range_top] narrow the range. Transitions may extend past the ends of the range; overlapping weights are normalized. Use [member debug_mode] to see the result. Does not require rebaking.

If [code]true[/code], uses a GPU-based denoising algorithm on the generated lightmap. This eliminates most noise within the generated lightmap at the cost of longer bake times. File sizes are generally not impacted significantly by the use of a denoiser, although lossless compression may do a better job at compressing a denoised image.

If [code]true[/code], a texture with the lighting information will be generated to speed up the generation of indirect lighting at the cost of some accuracy. The geometry might exhibit extra light leak artifacts when using low resolution lightmaps or UVs that stretch the lightmap significantly across surfaces. Leave [member use_texture_for_bounces] at its default value of [code]true[/code] if unsure. [b]Note:[/b] [member use_texture_for_bounces] only has an effect if [member bounces] is set to a value greater than or equal to [code]1[/code].

constants.constant: Bake lightmap textures and probe lighting together. This is the default mode.
Bake lightmap textures while retaining probe positions, topology and lighting. Existing probes are marked as needing a refresh on their [LightProbeSystem].
Bake probe lighting and update its topology while preserving lightmap textures, shadowmasks and mesh atlas assignments. Scene geometry and material preparation are still required.
A probe-only bake was requested but this node has no descendant [LightProbeSystem] belonging to it.

Low bake quality (fastest bake times). The quality of this preset can be adjusted by changing [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/bake_quality/low_quality_ray_count] and [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/bake_quality/low_quality_probe_ray_count].

Medium bake quality (fast bake times). The quality of this preset can be adjusted by changing [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/bake_quality/medium_quality_ray_count] and [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/bake_quality/medium_quality_probe_ray_count].

High bake quality (slow bake times). The quality of this preset can be adjusted by changing [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/bake_quality/high_quality_ray_count] and [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/bake_quality/high_quality_probe_ray_count].

Highest bake quality (slowest bake times). The quality of this preset can be adjusted by changing [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/bake_quality/ultra_quality_ray_count] and [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/bake_quality/ultra_quality_probe_ray_count].
Lightmap baking was successful.
Lightmap baking failed because the root node for the edited scene could not be accessed.
Lightmap baking failed as the lightmap data resource is embedded in a foreign resource.
Lightmap baking failed as there is no lightmapper available in this Godot build.
Lightmap baking failed as the [LightmapGIData] save path isn't configured in the resource.

Lightmap baking failed as there are no meshes whose [member GeometryInstance3D.gi_mode] is [constant GeometryInstance3D.GI_MODE_STATIC] and with valid UV2 mapping in the current scene. You may need to select 3D scenes in the Import dock and change their global illumination mode accordingly.
Lightmap baking failed as the lightmapper failed to analyze some of the meshes marked as static for baking.
Lightmap baking failed as the resulting image couldn't be saved or imported by Godot after it was saved.
The user aborted the lightmap baking operation (typically by clicking the [b]Cancel[/b] button in the progress dialog).
Lightmap baking failed as the maximum texture size is too small to fit some of the meshes marked for baking.
Lightmap baking failed as the lightmap is too small.
Lightmap baking failed as the lightmap was unable to fit into an atlas.
Ignore environment lighting when baking lightmaps.

Use the scene's environment lighting when baking lightmaps. [b]Note:[/b] If baking lightmaps in a scene with no [WorldEnvironment] node, this will act like [constant ENVIRONMENT_MODE_DISABLED]. The editor's preview sky and sun is [i]not[/i] taken into account by [LightmapGI] when baking lightmaps.
Use [member environment_custom_sky] as a source of environment lighting when baking lightmaps.
Use [member environment_custom_color] multiplied by [member environment_custom_energy] as a constant source of environment lighting when baking lightmaps.
Render normal lighting.
Show the shadows weight as a grayscale mask: white for full contribution and black for none.
Show the midtones weight as a grayscale mask: white for full contribution and black for none.
Show the highlights weight as a grayscale mask: white for full contribution and black for none.
